descriptionChirho: An interjection of prophetic denunciation or lamentation, introducing oracles of judgment against nations, cities, or social groups, overwhelmingly used in the prophetic literature (Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Amos, Habakkuk, Nahum, Zechariah). Carries a strong sense of impending doom or grief. Eng 'woe / Woe', spa 'Ay / Ay!', hin 'hay', arb 'waylun', kor 'hwa-isseuljineo', swa 'ole / Ole'.

An attention-getting interjection used as a summons or call, distinct from the woe-oracle usage. In Zechariah 2:10 (Eng 2:6), it calls people to flee from Babylon, functioning as a rallying cry rather than a denunciation. The multilingual evidence clearly differentiates this from the 'woe' sense: eng 'ho', spa 'Oh', hin 'he' (vocative particle), arb 'ya' (vocative particle), kor 'ora' (come!), swa 'Lo' (behold).
